actions.justification: Immediate stroke team activation is the first step in acute stroke management to mobilize resources and expedite care.
Last known well time is critical for determining eligibility for thrombolysis (tPA within 4.5h) and thrombectomy (within 24h) and must be obtained immediately.
NIHSS quantifies stroke severity, guides treatment decisions, and establishes a baseline neurological exam — mandatory early in stroke evaluation.
Stat CT head is the highest priority mandatory action for acute stroke - needed to rule out hemorrhagic stroke before any thrombolytic therapy can be considered. Must be completed urgently.
Mandatory action - hypoglycemia can mimic stroke symptoms and must be ruled out immediately. Critical safety check before treatment decisions.
Mandatory action - IV access is essential for medication administration, lab draws, and potential tPA administration in acute stroke workup.
Mandatory action - ECG is essential to identify atrial fibrillation or other cardiac sources of embolism in acute stroke workup.
Mandatory action - CBC, BMP, and coagulation studies are required to assess eligibility for thrombolysis, identify metabolic abnormalities, and guide treatment decisions.
Assessing pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale is important to establish baseline functional status and guide treatment eligibility and goals.
ASPECTS score should be assessed from the CT head to evaluate extent of early ischemic changes and guide eligibility for reperfusion therapy.
Early activation of the neurointerventional team is critical in case the patient is a candidate for mechanical thrombectomy, minimizing door-to-groin time.
Antiplatelet therapy assessment is needed as part of acute ischemic stroke management pathway, pending review of thrombolysis eligibility and imaging results.
Serial vital sign monitoring is essential to track hemodynamic stability and detect any deterioration in this stroke patient, even though initial vitals are stable.
Hyperglycemia worsens stroke outcomes; monitoring and maintaining euglycemia is a standard early intervention in acute stroke management.
Hyperthermia increases metabolic demand and worsens ischemic penumbra injury; temperature management is a key supportive care measure in acute stroke.

BP management targeting <180/105 is critical for stroke patients, especially if tPA is being considered. Current BP is 120/80 which is acceptable, but monitoring and management protocol should be established.
Patient requires admission to ICU or stroke unit for close neurological monitoring, serial assessments, and management of acute stroke while awaiting pending lab results and CT head findings.
